# go-libfossil

> A Fossil repository engine in Go without cgo: it reads, writes and syncs Fossil repositories (the artifact format, the derived tables and the sync protocol). Go module `github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil` (package `libfossil`), command `libfossil`. A repository is an ordinary `.fossil` SQLite file that stock fossil reads.

This file is generated from `docs/site/llms-header.md` plus the docs site. Every link below is a page on the docs site; [llms-full.txt](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/llms-full.txt) holds all pages in one file.

## Key concepts

- **Artifact**: a text manifest made of cards (check-in, tag, wiki, cluster, ...). Its name is the SHA1 or SHA3-256 hash of its bytes.
- **Repository state**: the tables (`event`, `plink`, `mlink`, `tagxref`, `leaf`, ...) derived from the artifacts by crosslinking, matching what `fossil rebuild` writes.
- **Sync**: Fossil's card protocol over HTTP (`igot`, `gimme`, `file`, ...), as a client (`Clone`, `Repo.Sync`, `Repo.Pull`) and a stateless server (`libfossil repo serve`).
- **Sparse cone**: a set of paths a checkout or a store holds; content outside it is elided, not lost.
- **Horizon**: a check-in below which a store leaves history on the origin; at the structural depth the clone verifies a seed the origin can sign.
- **Sub-manifests**: an extension that writes a check-in as a tree of manifests instead of one flat file list, shared with zit.
- **Driver**: the `database/sql` SQLite driver, chosen by blank import: `db/driver/modernc` (pure Go) or `db/driver/ncruces` (SQLite as WebAssembly, for js/wasm and wasip1).

## Quick start

1. `go install github.com/danmestas/go-libfossil/cmd/libfossil@latest`
2. `libfossil repo new notes.fossil`, then `libfossil -R notes.fossil repo open .`, `libfossil repo add README.md`, `libfossil repo ci -m "first notes"`.
3. From Go: blank-import a driver, then `libfossil.Create(path, libfossil.CreateOpts{User: "ana"})` or `libfossil.Open(path)`, and `r.Commit(libfossil.CommitOpts{...})`, `r.Timeline(libfossil.TimelineOpts{...})`.
4. Sync: `libfossil.Clone(ctx, path, libfossil.NewHTTPTransport(url), libfossil.CloneOpts{})`, then `r.Sync(ctx, t, libfossil.SyncOpts{Pull: true})`.

## Go packages

- `.` (package `libfossil`): `Repo`, `Create`, `Open`, `Clone`, check-ins, checkouts, history, merge, sync.
- `cli`: the Kong command structs behind `libfossil`, embeddable in another binary.
- `db`: the SQLite abstraction and driver registration.
- `db/driver/modernc`: pure-Go SQLite driver (separate module).
- `db/driver/ncruces`: SQLite-as-WebAssembly driver (separate module).
- `observer/otel`: OpenTelemetry observer (separate module).
- `dst`: deterministic simulation of sync between nodes.
- `simio`: clock, randomness and storage seams for deterministic tests.

## Get started

- [Install](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/install/): go-libfossil is a Go module and a command.
- [Quickstart: the CLI](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/quickstart/): Create a repository, commit a file, and read the result with stock fossil.
- [Embed in Go](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/embed-in-go/): The libfossil package does what the command does, as typed Go values instead of command output.
- [First sync](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/get-started/first-sync/): Two repositories exchange check-ins with Fossil's sync protocol over HTTP.

## Concepts

- [Architecture](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/architecture/): The packages of go-libfossil, the SQLite driver layer, the observer interfaces and the deterministic simulator.
- [Artifacts](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/artifacts/): Everything a Fossil repository records is an artifact: a run of bytes, named by its own hash, that is never changed once written.
- [Repository state](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/repository-state/): Artifacts are the only facts a repository records.
- [Sync](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/sync/): Two repositories exchange artifacts with Fossil's sync protocol: text cards carried in HTTP POST bodies, one request and one reply per round.
- [Sub-manifests](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/sub-manifests/): A check-in manifest has one F card per file in the tree, not per changed file.
- [Sparse cones](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/sparse-cones/): A repository does not have to hold everything.
- [Horizons](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/horizons/): A horizon cuts a store by time.
- [Signing](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/concepts/signing/): go-libfossil signs two kinds of artifact: check-ins, as fossil and zit sign them, and the seeds an origin mints for structural horizons.

## Guides

- [Production patterns](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/guides/production/): The Quickstart uses log.Fatal to keep the snippets short.
- [Migrating from fossil](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/guides/migrating-from-fossil/): This guide is for users of upstream Fossil SCM (the C binary distributed by fossil-scm.org) who are evaluating libfossil — a pure-Go implementation of the Fossil repository format and sync protocol.
- [Embedding the CLI](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/guides/cli-embedding/): An application that keeps version history in a Fossil repository can run the libfossil binary as a child process: no checkout, no shadow working tree.
- [Extension points](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/guides/extension-points/): libfossil exposes four surfaces for consumers that want to instrument, extend, or replace pieces of the stack:
- [Testing](https://libfossil-docs.daniel-mestas.workers.dev/docs/guides/testing/): This guide describes libfossil's test strategy for contributors adding tests or investigating failures.
